subject.company: Eli Lilly and Company and Novo Nordisk A/S
subject.research_question: Among the current LLY and NVO positive PEAD candidates mapped to the same downstream decision date, can source-dated incretin demand converted into net revenue after price and mix effects identify the stronger H10/H20 replacement-value candidate?

researchability.basis: Issuer and regulator primary sources establish a plausible demand-to-revenue conversion mechanism and both current PEAD rows are hash-bound, but the companies disclose volume, price, currency, rebate and product mix on incompatible levels and only one paired decision date is visible. The card is therefore lead-only and cannot establish a trade or Gate claim.
limitations: Lilly's numeric price-volume bridge is mainly company- and region-level, while Novo reports CER, adjusted sales, therapy-area sales and partially estimated prescription data; the values cannot be directly ranked as product-level unit economics.
Novo published on 2026-08-04 and Lilly on 2026-08-05, so the issuer-specific updates are not one common exogenous shock even though the local PEAD rows map to the same 2026-08-06 decision date.
Only one independent LLY-NVO paired decision date is bound, versus the preregistered minimum of five executable pair dates in every canonical window.
Canonical historical as-known product-level volume, price, mix, rebate and decision-price vintages are unavailable.
No pair-matched derivatives, positioning, factor, covariance or independent observable market-prior cohort is bound.
Current live position control blocks new entries because EXIT_NOW and unconfirmed manual bracket conditions remain active.

business_analyst.conclusion: Lilly currently shows the clearer commercial conversion from incretin demand into reported revenue despite realized-price pressure; Novo also shows strong demand, especially for oral Wegovy, but its net-sales conversion is more visibly diluted by price, rebate, geography and channel mix. This is a mechanism lead only, not a company recommendation or admission decision.

evidence.claim: Lilly reported Q2 2026 revenue growth of 48%, with volume contributing 60% and realized prices subtracting 13%; Mounjaro and Zepbound revenue increased 91% and 46%, respectively.

Novo reported Q2 adjusted sales growth of 7% at CER, driven by GLP-1 volume growth and a favorable U.S. rebate adjustment but partly offset by lower realized prices; weekly Wegovy pill prescriptions exceeded 265,000.
Both issuers are expanding manufacturing, but the disclosed projects phase in over years and do not provide comparable current utilization or standard-dose output for an H10/H20 causal claim.

FDA had already determined that national tirzepatide and semaglutide injection supply could meet current and projected U.S. demand, so nationwide shortage resolution alone cannot distinguish the two candidates, although local disruption can remain.

business_analyst.uncertainty: The source pack lacks a common geography, indication, dose, sell-through definition and net-revenue-per-unit bridge. Channel fill, rebate-estimate changes and launch mix can make reported revenue growth look like physical capacity conversion when it is not. The mechanism is falsified if comparable product-level data show Novo retains at least as much net revenue per incremental unit as Lilly.

financial_analyst.conclusion: Lilly's current incretin revenue conversion is stronger and more directly quantifiable, but the disclosed inputs do not prove a unit-volume advantage. Lilly's Mounjaro plus Zepbound Q2 revenue rose 73.32% year over year, while Novo's current four-product incretin total is not a comparable growth rate because oral Wegovy lacks a prior-year base and the company does not publish a numeric product-level volume-price bridge.

evidence.claim: Lilly Q2 Mounjaro plus Zepbound revenue was $14,871 million versus $8,580 million a year earlier; (14,871 / 8,580 - 1) x 100 = 73.32%. This is brand revenue growth, not unit-volume growth.
Lilly's Q2 total revenue was $22,974 million versus $15,558 million; (22,974 / 15,558 - 1) x 100 = 47.67%, consistent with the reported 48%, while gross margin was 85.8%, up 1.5 percentage points.

Novo Q2 incretin product revenue totaled DKK 59,305 million: Ozempic 31,375, oral semaglutide 5,228, injectable Wegovy 19,484 and Wegovy pill 3,218; the new pill has no prior-year base and the other disclosed CER growth rates do not form a common unit-volume bridge.

Novo's adjusted Q2 operating profit margin was 33,389 / 78,488 = 42.54%, but it is not comparable with Lilly's gross margin because the measures are at different profit-stack levels and use different currency and adjustment conventions.

financial_analyst.uncertainty: Lilly does not disclose a tirzepatide-specific numeric unit-price bridge and Novo does not disclose a product-level numeric volume-price bridge. CER, 340B adjustments, rebates, currencies, launch bases and product mix prevent direct ranking. The lead is falsified if a same-definition product bridge shows Lilly's incremental unit growth or net-revenue retention is no better than Novo's.

industry_researcher.conclusion: The global incretin market remains concentrated around Lilly and Novo, but competition now turns on dosage form, access, net price, channel inventory and manufacturing ramp rather than a simple nationwide-shortage binary. Current primary sources support faster Lilly revenue conversion, not superior physical capacity efficiency, and the two earnings releases are issuer-specific events rather than a synchronized external shock.

evidence.claim: FDA's national shortage decisions cover U.S. aggregate supply and still allow localized supply disruptions; therefore shortage status cannot stand in for company-level sell-through or capacity utilization.

Novo reported global obesity sales of DKK 23,152 million, up 16% at CER, while cited U.S. obesity market volume growth was 87% and its U.S. obesity sales grew only 4% at CER, illustrating why volume and reported sales need an explicit price and mix bridge.

Lilly reported volume growth of 37% in the U.S. and 113% outside the U.S., with realized-price declines of 3% and 36%, respectively, showing that geography and reimbursement materially change demand-to-revenue conversion.

Novo's announcement was timestamped 2026-08-04T16:37:02Z, while Lilly's earnings call occurred on 2026-08-05 at 10:00 EDT; the local shared decision date does not establish one common information shock.

industry_researcher.uncertainty: Issuer-cited IQVIA data use different regions, dates, denominators and self-pay estimates. Neither company discloses a common standard-dose output, utilization, inventory or net-price-per-dose series. The industry relation is falsified if comparable contemporaneous sell-through data show Novo's conversion is not weaker or if one common regulator event, rather than issuer-specific releases, explains both candidates.

risk_assessor.conclusion: The pair is sufficiently timestamped to freeze a lead, but not to run an admissible historical treatment. One pair date, incompatible issuer fields, absent canonical historical vintages, no independent market-prior cohort and no validated transmission to H10/H20 force fail-closed D0-D3. Current live controls independently require no trade.

evidence.claim: The frozen local snapshot contains exactly one LLY-NVO pair date, with LLY PEAD rank 1 and NVO rank 3, and explicitly records that no settled outcomes were read.
The frozen scope labels the pair surface research_pit, the issuer comparison snapshot_only, and requires five independent pair decisions in every standard window before any Gate claim.
Current position control has ok_to_add_control_pass=false because EXIT_NOW and manual bracket orders not confirmed by the broker remain active, so portfolio cash does not create execution authority.
The dynamic readiness artifact has zero ready registered lanes; derivatives, positioning and paired settlement evidence therefore cannot be borrowed to support this candidate.

risk_assessor.uncertainty: Historical disclosure mappings, revision behavior, event clocks, product definitions, pair-touch density, issuer concentration, factor and portfolio covariance are unresolved. Any replay using current restated mappings or non-comparable issuer fields would be not_pit rather than admissible research_pit.

decision.rationale: All four roles completed with source-dated evidence and agree the demand-to-revenue conversion question is coherent enough to submit as a lead. They also agree that product-level comparability, common event timing, historical PIT, touch density, market prior, transmission, novelty, concentration and replacement value remain exclusively for authoritative D0-D3 qualification, without override or trade authority.

candidate.title: LLY-NVO PEAD demand-to-revenue conversion ranking lead
candidate.hypothesis: For the current LLY and NVO positive PEAD candidates mapped to the same downstream decision date, a source-dated and consistently defined product-level incretin volume-growth measure net of price and mix effects may identify the more durable post-earnings drift candidate; keep PEAD eligibility unchanged, use its score only as a deterministic tie-breaker, and evaluate at most one long common-equity candidate from the next regular-session open over fixed H10 and H20 replacement value.
candidate.why_not_arbitraged: Both earnings headlines and price responses are public. A residual edge can exist only if the market incompletely maps comparable product-level volume, net-price and supply conversion into relative H10/H20 cash flows, and it must survive PIT, density, transmission, concentration and exact opportunity-cost tests.
candidate.falsifier: Reject or park if issuer fields cannot be aligned by product, geography, currency convention and known_at; if the updates are treated as one common shock; if any standard window has fewer than five independent executable pair dates; if no valid novelty axis survives; if H10 and H20 replacement value does not beat cash, SPY, QQQ, unconditioned PEAD and the unselected pair member after costs; or if one issuer contributes more than 40% of positive treatment value.

baseline.policy: Use the current broad-universe EPS-surprise-only PEAD eligibility and score ordering with its frozen universe, next-open clock, notional, costs and exits.

treatment.policy: Keep PEAD eligibility unchanged. Only when both issuers have source-dated, same-definition product-level volume growth and price-or-mix contribution known before the decision open, rank the pair by volume-led incretin growth net of price and mix drag; use the existing PEAD score only as a deterministic tie-breaker, otherwise abstain. Evaluate fixed H10 and H20 horizons.

candidate.replacement_value_comparator: Zero-return cash, identical-interval SPY and QQQ, the exact unconditioned PEAD ordering, and the unselected pair member at the same decision clock, notional, costs and exit policy.

execution_envelope.intended_instrument: At most one of LLY or NVO common stock; no pair short, option, leverage, inverse product or proxy mapping
execution_envelope.liquidity_dependency: Canonical equity liquidity, gap-cancel, stale-price and FX-normalization controls must pass at the next regular-session open
execution_envelope.costs_and_carry: Repository cash-equity commissions and slippage at identical notional; no financing or borrow credit
execution_envelope.capacity_constraint: At most one existing PEAD candidate slot, issuer positive-contribution concentration below 40%, no portfolio allocation and no production effect
execution_envelope.timing_constraint: Consensus, event, product-level volume, price or mix, supply and signal-day price inputs must all be source-dated and known before the simulated entry open
